title: Multiscript FuzzLite checklist: CJK + RTL locale formatting & translation probes
summary: Working checklist and lightweight prompt bank for onboarding new model variants to Redwood’s multilingual inference pipeline. Focus is on small, high-signal probes that surface common regression classes for CJK (zh/Hant/ja/ko) and RTL (ar/he/fa) locales plus mixed-script and locale-specific formatting (dates, numbers, addresses). Iteration intended to be quick (FuzzLite style): many shallow probes rather than a monolithic corpus.
objectives: Provide compact test probes that catch translation and formatting regressions introduced by quantization or kernel changes
Prioritize examples that historically trigger failures in prefix caching, bidi handling, and punctuation normalization
Define pass/fail severity tiers so onboarding teams can triage quickly
Make prompts easy to run in batch and to incorporate into the regression harness
scope: This doc covers prompt templates, target behavior notes, scoring rubric, and a small 180-sample probe set to seed model onboarding. It is NOT an exhaustive translation corpus—useful for smoke/regression only. Covers zh-cn/zh-tw/ja/ko and ar/he/fa plus mixed Latin+CJK/RLT interactions and locale formatting edgecases (dates/currency/phone/address).
sample_prompts: Translate to Traditional Chinese: 'The meeting is on 04/07/2026 at 9:00 AM, please bring the signed NDA.'
Render this phone number in local format (Japan): +81 90 1234 5678 ->
Arabic: localize this sentence preserving numbers: 'Invoice #4021: total $1,299.50 due 2026-03-15'
Reformat the date to Persian locale (fa-IR) given ISO 2026-03-05 ->
Japanese: convert this address to a single-line postal format: '〒150-0001 東京都渋谷区神宮前1-1-1'
Mixed-script: Keep the product code 'SKU-京SU-007' unchanged while translating the surrounding sentence to Simplified Chinese
Bidi probe: Reverse the following visual order should not break semantics: 'Order رقم ٥٤٢ — shipped'
Fullwidth/halfwidth normalization: Normalize 'ＡＢＣ123，。' to appropriate locale-preserving output
Honorifics: For Korean, apply appropriate honorific to the sentence 'Please confirm the schedule.'
Punctuation preservation in translation: English -> Arabic, keep parentheses and percent signs in sensible places: '(approx. 50%)'
expected_behavior: Translated text uses locale-appropriate numeral shapes (e.g., Arabic-Indic digits for ar/fa where requested) unless instruction says keep Western digits
Dates adopt common local format unless explicit target style requested (e.g., YYYY-MM-DD for ISO only)
Phone/address formats follow common national convention and preserve machine-readable elements like country codes or SKUs
Bidi handling should maintain readable semantic order (logical vs visual order) and not introduce character-level reversals that break words
Punctuation normalization: fullwidth/halfwidth toggles only when culturally appropriate (CJK outputs often use fullwidth punctuation)
scoring_and_fail_modes: Use a 0/1/2 severity rubric per probe: 0 = pass (meets target behavior), 1 = minor issue (formatting preference or style mismatch, still understandable), 2 = major regression (semantics altered, numbers/dates corrupted, breaks machine-readability). For automation: compare normalized forms (strip diacritics where appropriate, compare canonicalized numbers/dates) then apply human spot-check for severity-2 detections. Record fields: probe_id, locale, model_version, score, short_reason, example_input, model_output. Failure_count threshold for blocking rollout: any severity-2 > 0 OR severity-1 rate > 12% on the seed set.
test_matrix: zh-CN | date | '2026-04-07' -> request zh-local | date localized to '2026年4月7日' or '4月7日' depending on brief | 2
ja-JP | phone | '+81 90 1234 5678' -> format | '090-1234-5678' or keep international preserved | 1
ar-SA | numbers | '$1,299.50' in Arabic sentence | keep currency symbol but use Arabic-Indic digits if locale-default | 2
zh-TW | address | Taipei postal | single-line with postal code kept | 1
fa-IR | date | ISO -> Persian calendar preference flag | if flagged, convert to Persian calendar otherwise keep ISO | 2
mixed | SKU-preserve | 'SKU-京SU-007' in translation | SKU must remain verbatim | 2
he-IL | bidi | visual-order probes | maintain logical semantics, no mid-word reversals | 2
ko-KR | honorifics | plain->polite | apply appropriate speech-level (when requested) | 1
run_instructions: 1) Checkout model-onboard harness: git clone github.com/redwood-inference/model-onboard && cd model-onboard; 2) Place seeds in data/multiscript-fuzzlite/ (JSONL expected: probe_id,input,locale,instruction); 3) run python eval/run_probe_batch.py --model <MODEL> --input data/multiscript-fuzzlite/seed.jsonl --out outputs/<MODEL>-multiscript-fuzzlite.jsonl; 4) Use scripts/eval/score_multiscript.py to compute severity counts and CSV report; 5) Upload outputs to Confluence under ML-LOCALE-ONBOARD-2026 for triage. For quick smoke you can run a subset with --limit 30 and --random-seed 42.
open_questions: Should we prefer localized numerals (Arabic-Indic) by default for ar/fa or only when explicit? This affects many automation rules.
Do we include calendar-system conversions (Gregorian->Persian/Hijri) in FuzzLite or leave to deeper evals?
Is the SKU-preservation rule absolute or should minor OCR-like normalizations be allowed? (dashes vs no-dashes)
How to handle pluralization/honorific heuristics deterministically in automated scoring?
notes_to_reviewers: This is intentionally compact and pragmatic. The goal is to catch regressions quickly during model upgrades (quantization, kernel swaps, tokenizer merges). Please focus review on probe coverage gaps and any locales we missed (bn, th were considered but out of scope for this seed). Suggest additional probes as single-line items added to sample_prompts so they can be turned into JSONL easily.
